title: Continuous cochains form a delta-functor
statement: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group and $A$ a finite ring. Let $\mathcal C$ be the abelian category of left $A$-modules with $A$-linear $G$-action and open stabilizers [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. There is a functor $F:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(A\text{-Mod},\mathbb N)$ whose degree-$n$ term is naturally linearly equivalent to $\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$, with $M$ discrete. Its coefficient maps are postcomposition by equivariant linear maps. Its differential is $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$. There is a cohomological delta-functor $T$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] with $T^q=F\circ H^q$ in every degree. No effaceability or derived-invariants comparison is asserted.

proof.text: Construct continuous cochain terms and differentials explicitly. Continuity of the action follows from open stabilizers; finite sums preserve continuity. The bar differential squares to zero by pairwise cancellation. Postcomposition commutes with the differential. Linearity implies additivity of the resulting functors.

Apply continuousCochains_shortExact to each short exact coefficient sequence. Its term equivalences give cochain isomorphisms to the constructed complexes, since both differentials have the specified formula. These isomorphisms identify the induced arrows by postcomposition and transfer short exactness. The homology sequence supplies connecting maps and exactness at each position, and homology sequence naturality supplies the connecting-map axiom. In degree zero there are no incoming boundaries, so an injective cochain map induces an injective homology map. These maps and additive homology functors give the asserted delta-functor.
